description.narrative:
Statistics on international migration between African countries and out of Africa are compiled by the African Union Commission, STATAFRIC, the UN Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA), the International Labour Organisation (ILO), the International Organisation for Migration (IOM), Regional Economic Communities (RECs) and by government and private national institutions. Although some improvements have taken place in the last years, migration statistics in Africa generally suffers from poor quality, poorly aligned data collection periods, unharmonised definitions and standards, lacking possibilities to use administrative data sources and a low level of cooperation and data sharing between national data producers.
Quality statistics on migration, mobility and displacement are fundamental to the implementation of adequate policies on migration at national, regional, and continental level. Yet, in many countries, even the most general statistics on migration are incomplete, out-of-date or do not exist. Improvement in this area requires knowledge of the principles of collecting, compiling and analyzing migration statistics. Likewise, policymakers and other users need to be aware of the definitions and measurement issues related to the data to be able to interpret them.
The Migration Statistics II project contributes to improving the availability of relevant and good quality statistics on migration in Africa for use in decision- and policymaking on migration issues.
The second phase of Migration Statistics II relies on the significant work done in Capacity Development in Migration Statistics which was implemented over the period January 2019- December 2022.

Statistik om migration mellan afrikanska länder och ut ur Afrika sammanställs av Afrikanska Unionens institut för statistik, STATAFRIC, samt av FN:s Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA), International Labour Organisation (ILO), International Organisation for Migration (IOM), Regional Economic Communities (RECs) och av statliga och privata nationella institutioner. Även om vissa förbättringar har skett under de senaste åren lider migrationsstatistiken i Afrika i allmänhet av dålig kvalitet, bristfälligt koordinerade insamlingsperioder, oharmoniserade definitioner och standarder, bristande möjligheter att använda administrativa datakällor och en låg nivå av samarbete och datadelning mellan nationella dataproducenter. Kvalitetsstatistik om migration och rörlighet är grundläggande för genomförandet av adekvata migrationsstrategier på nationell, regional och kontinental nivå men i många länder är även den mest grundläggande statistiken om migration ofullständig, inaktuell eller existerar inte. Förbättringar på detta område kräver kunskap om principerna för insamling, sammanställning och analys av migrationsstatistik. Likaså måste beslutsfattare och andra användare vara medvetna om definitionerna och mätproblem relaterade till data för att kunna tolka densamma. Projektet Migration Statistics II bidrar till att förbättra tillgången till relevant statistik av god kvalitet om migration i Afrika för användning i policyutformning och beslutsfattande avseende migration.
Den andra fasen av programmet bygger på det betydande arbete som gjorts genomförts under programmets första fas, Capacity Development in Migration Statistics, som implementerades under perioden januari 2019–december 2022.

The project objective is increased availability of high-quality migration statistics to users enabling adequate management of the effects of migration on women and men, girls and boys. In addition, the migration statistics will be used to monitor and evaluate the continental and international agendas such as Agenda 2063, Agenda 2030 and Global Compact on Migration.
The project will strengthen the capacity of STATAFRIC, RECs and Member States to produce, harmonize and disseminate migration statistics. This will be achieved through the implementation of capacity development activities leading to tangible results. Thus, five components have been identified (with the first four from the first phase of the project) completed by a new fifth component:
Component 1: Statistics production
Component 2: Concepts and methods
Component 3: Dissemination and publication
Component 4: Coordination
Component 5: Forced displacement
The project will consolidate the results obtained during the first phase of Capacity Development for Migration Statistics and to support STATAFRIC and the selected RECs in the implementation of continental and regional statistical plans. The project will be funded by Sida.

Component 1: Statistics Production STATAFRIC validated and published the fourth edition of the Labour Migration Statistics Report in Africa (LMSRA), officially launched on 31 July 2026. An internal production process was established to support regular reporting, and a harmonized data collection questionnaire was developed and validated in December 2025. RECs further strengthened regional reporting. IGAD and EAC published the second and third editions of their regional migration reports, respectively. COMESA and AMU advanced preparations for their second editions, while ECCAS completed the first draft of its inaugural regional migration report. AMU also established structures to support regular report production. Migration data systems were strengthened through the establishment or enhancement of secure databases at STATAFRIC, AMU, and IGAD, while ECOWAS advanced work towards a regional migration database. Progress was also made in strengthening sex-disaggregated and gender-responsive statistics. STATAFRIC integrated a gender perspective into its data collection tools, EAC and IGAD finalized Gender Statistics Strategies, and COMESA formalized collaboration with its Gender Division to support gender sensitive reporting.
Component 2: Concepts and Methods STATAFRIC finalized the continental Guidelines on Migration and Displacement Statistics, which were subsequently validated by the Statistical Technical Group (STG). The guidelines provide a common framework for harmonizing migration and displacement statistics across Africa. Following their validation, RECs initiated or advanced the development of regional guidelines aligned with the continental framework. EAC developed and endorsed regional guidelines aligned with AU and UN standards. IGAD engaged member states in the review and refinement of draft guidelines to ensure consistency with national contexts and continental standards. COMESA strengthened member state engagement through National Technical Working Group (NTWG) workshops focused on harmonized concepts, definitions, and methodologies. The guideline development process also facilitated knowledge exchange among member states, strengthened coordination among national institutions, and helped identify common challenges in migration data production.
Component 3: Dissemination and Publication Migration statistics has increasingly become integrated into continental and regional publications and dissemination platforms. STATAFRIC published and launched the fourth edition of the LMSRA and advanced the development of a continental migration data portal and a Migration Data Profile Report. At the regional level, IGAD launched the second edition of its Migration Statistics Report and integrated migration statistics into its Statistics Yearbook. EAC incorporated migration indicators into its Facts and Figures publication. COMESA published updated migration statistics through its COMSTAT platform, including gender-responsive analysis. ECCAS finalized its first regional migration report, while ECOWAS advanced preparations for the third edition of its report. Dissemination systems were further strengthened through the operationalization of migration data portals and the development of similar platforms in COMESA, EAC, and ECOWAS, improving access to migration statistics for policymakers and other stakeholders.
Component 4: Coordination The coordination architecture for migration statistics has become further institutionalized. STATAFRIC integrated biannual STG meetings into the continental statistical governance framework, establishing a permanent coordination mechanism. Regional Technical Working Groups (RTWGs) continued to coordinate migration statistics activities and maintain linkages with NTWGs. Support was provided to establish or strengthen NTWGs in several member states, including Libya, Equatorial Guinea, Mauritius, Seychelles, Kenya, Ethiopia, South Sudan, Djibouti, and Somalia. InterREC collaboration, statistical exchanges, and joint technical activities strengthened knowledge sharing and coordination. Partnerships with IOM, ILO, EGRISS, and the African Migration Observatory (AMO) supported capacity-building initiatives, including the Fourth School on Migration Statistics and the development of statistical guidelines. Several RECs, including AMU, ECOWAS, and COMESA, explored options for securing long-term technical and financial support for migration statistics activities beyond project-based funding. Institutional integration was further reflected in developments such as the appointment of IGAD's Migration Statistics Officer as Head of Statistics.
Component 5: Forced Displacement The 2025 edition of the LMSRA and regional migration reports included dedicated sections on forced displacement, drawing on EGRISS standards and methodologies. Capacity-building activities supported the integration of refugee, IDP, and statelessness statistics into national and regional statistical systems. EAC continued supporting member states, AMU developed a national implementation roadmap, ECCAS facilitated knowledge exchange, and ECOWAS expanded technical guidance. COMESA incorporated forced displacement statistics into NTWG workshops, promoting harmonized concepts and classifications. IGAD organized a dedicated report writing workshop with UNHCR support and strengthened its RTWG Sub Working Group on Displacement Statistics through the adoption of Terms of Reference and a regional roadmap.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
